issues.quote: After a new CFIUS review that he had ordered, on June 13, 2025, President Trump issued an order allowing it
issues.problem: The previous sentence is about Biden, so 'he' comes before Trump is named. A listener can hear it as Biden ordering the new CFIUS review. That would credit the wrong president with an official act. CRS says Trump ordered it.
issues.fix: President Trump then ordered a new CFIUS review, and on June 13, 2025, he issued an order allowing the acquisition, on the condition of a national security agreement.

issues.quote: Melting scrap in an electric arc furnace released about zero point seven. Per tonne of crude steel, less than a third of the emissions.
issues.problem: The worldsteel figures include indirect emissions, but CBAM counts only direct ones. The next paragraph puts '82 euros per tonne of CO2' and 'how a tonne of steel was made can change what it costs' right after these figures. Listeners are invited to do the 2.3 × 82 sum that was removed as C51 for mixing bases.
issues.fix: After 'less than a third of the emissions.' add: 'These World Steel averages also count indirect emissions, such as from purchased electricity, so they aren't the figures CBAM counts for steel.' Add to claims as a fact sourced to WSIF methodology + CBAMR Annex II (the C51 note already documents it).

issues.rule: §2 (opinion must fit the facts it explains)
issues.quote: One explanation: much of the world was still rebuilding after the war — an unusual moment, not a baseline.
issues.problem: The explanation follows the 1944 figure, but in 1944 the war was still going on, so 'rebuilding after the war' doesn't explain that year. It fits only 1950.
issues.fix: One explanation for the 1950 figure: much of the world was still rebuilding after the war — an unusual moment, not a baseline.

issues.rule: G §2 (memoir statements stay as the author wrote them)
issues.problem: The source says 'we decided' (Carnegie and his partners). The script turns it into a solo decision and drops the memoir attribution.
issues.fix: Around 1872, Carnegie recalled, he and his partners decided to build.

issues.problem: C31 covers only the quote 'weakening our internal economy' and the 80 % target. The table doesn't record that P9705 links the finding to global excess capacity.
issues.fix: Check the P9705 wording and add it to C31 as a verbatim quote. If it can't be confirmed in the text, cut 'together with global excess capacity,'.

issues.quote: a tariff sorts steel mainly by whether it crosses the border and what product it is.
issues.problem: The script itself reports tariffs that differ by country (Canada/Mexico exemption, UK rate) and EU quotas. Leaving out origin contradicts segments 07–08.
issues.fix: a tariff sorts steel mainly by where it comes from and what product it is.

issues.rule: G §1 / §6 (causality only where a source states it; no judging policy outcomes)
issues.quote: A tariff, a quota and a golden share each affect, in different ways, how much of that path stays inside a given border.
issues.problem: This states an effect. Segment 07 reports that CRS found studies of tariff effects reached different conclusions, so the line goes further than the record.
issues.fix: A tariff, a quota and a golden share each set terms, in different ways, for how steel moves across a given border.

issues.rule: G §5 / §1 (live event, operating company, financial condition)
issues.quote: As of October 2026, the latest: on September 30, Tech.eu and Finwire reported that Stegra's cost to complete the plant was "significantly higher than assumed in June" and that it needs more capital
issues.problem: This is fast-moving financial news about an operating company, sourced to press only. The original Stegra release has not been read (STG2 note). G §5 requires a status re-check before recording.
issues.fix: Action: before recording, re-check stegra.com, Cision and the press for newer updates (financing, CEO, timeline) and log the result with the date in claims.md. If the original release is found, cite it as well. Keep the 'reported' wording.

issues.quote: In 1950, America made about eighty-eight million tonnes of steel — almost half the world's. In 2025: about eighty-two million.
issues.problem: The narration compares USGS 'raw steel' with worldsteel 'crude steel' and only the screen discloses it. C02 requires the label in segments 00, 06 and 13.
issues.fix: Action: confirm the on-screen line 'USGS "raw steel" 1950 · worldsteel "crude steel" 2025' appears in the 00 and 13 frames, not just in 06.

issues.quote: The OECD projects the unused part to reach seven hundred forty-five million tonnes by 2028.
issues.problem: The narration labels it as a projection correctly. The visual also has to carry the PROJECTION label (C36).
issues.fix: Action: on screen, show 'PROJECTION — OECD Steel Outlook 2026' with a dashed line for the 2028 value.
